Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image appear to be a drawing made from chalk?
node.criteria: Pass if the edited image as a whole has the appearance of a chalk-made drawing. Fail if it clearly does not have that appearance, including when it shows only an unrelated edit or a partial chalk effect. Unknown if the edited image is unavailable or the appearance cannot be determined.
node.binding: O1: Judge the edited image against the requested outcome of a chalk drawing; supporting evidence does not independently earn completion credit.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image has a visibly drawn, grainy, chalk-like texture across the giraffes and background, giving the image as a whole the appearance of a chalk drawing.

fulfillment: The node’s completion rule is too permissive: it treats a grainy, chalk-like texture as sufficient proof that the whole image is a chalk drawing. In the edited image, the giraffes and scene remain recognizable, but the result also has a soft, blurred/painterly appearance; the trace does not establish that the requested medium is convincingly chalk rather than a partial or ambiguous stylization. Refine support 1 to assess the overall rendered medium against the source and distinguish a chalk-made drawing from merely chalk-like texture, without requiring any particular visual detail. Because support 1 passed with high confidence and caused support 2 to be skipped, inspect whether that criterion or its binding is collapsing partial progress into completion; do not treat the skipped support as negative evidence. Keep the partial/no distinction tied to observed requested progress, and leave the outcome unresolved if the visual evidence cannot distinguish completion from partial transformation. The reference label is an aggregate constraint, not atomic ground truth.

In this image, the giraffes and scene remain recognizable, with visible grain and softened, painterly/blurred rendering; that supports some requested progress but does not by itself establish completion. Calibrate the pass threshold to the overall medium transformation, while allowing a clear partial judgment when progress is visible but completion is not established, and leave it unresolved when the visual evidence is genuinely indeterminate. Treat the high-confidence pass as a possible criterion/binding calibration failure, not as proof of completion; the skipped downstream support is not negative evidence.
